messages:
Ashley: Heads-up — since ~03:12 UTC we're seeing intermittent packet loss on east-west between gpu nodes in us-west-2. Affected pods are streaming model checkpoints (grpc) and keep hitting short stalls/stream resets. Seen across two AZs (a/b).
Devon: Any pattern on node pairs? same rack, same NIC type?
Ashley: Mixed. Mostly between nodes on different racks but same instance type (g5-like). Not all pairs, seems bursty every ~5–15m.
Ravi: Can you grab a quick iperf3 and a tcpdump on the host side? Also run `ip -s link` for the geneve/tunnel iface. Suspect offload edge cases.
Ashley: running now.
Ashley: iperf3 between node1 -> node2: short tests show ~10–15ms spikes and a few retransmits.
Ashley: tcpdump (capturing geneve UDP 6081) shows repeated duplicated outer headers then inner syns getting no reply. snippet:
```
12:03:14.123456 IP 10.1.2.3.51820 > 10.2.3.4.6081: Geneve, v0, proto 0x6558, options 0x0, length 1500
12:03:14.123460 IP 10.1.2.3.51820 > 10.2.3.4.6081: Geneve, v0, proto 0x6558, length 54
```
Devon: interesting — outer UDP delivered but inner small packets look lost. what's MTU on geneve and the physical links?
Ashley: physical NICs are MTU 9000, geneve iface shows MTU 1450 (we set low for historical reasons).
Ravi: That MTU mismatch could punish offloads. Also check `ethtool -k` on the NICs and tunnel: GSO/GRO/TSO state. Some drivers mishandle GSO when tunnel MTU < path MTU.
Caleb: run `sudo ethtool -K <iface> gso off gro off tso off` on one side and re-run short iperf. It's an ugly workaround but can reveal if offload is culprit.
Ashley: did that on node1: disabled offloads on geneve0 and the physical eth. iperf jitter dropped and the small-packet loss went away for the 10m test window.
Devon: good repro. That points at offload/kernel/driver interaction. Any recent kernel or NIC firmware changes on that fleet?
Ashley: nodes were on kernel 5.10.95 -> 5.10.102 rolled two days ago to pick up security fixes. Firmware unchanged. Correlation looks plausible.
Ravi: capture `ip -s link show geneve0` before/after. Also collect `dmesg | grep -i -e eth -e mlx -e firmware -e geneve` and incr counters for `ip -s link`.
Ashley: pasted `ip -s link show geneve0` output: RX: 0 errors, 134 dropped, TX: 0 errors, 0 dropped.
Caleb: dropping on RX of geneve suggests kernel delivered outer but failed to reassemble inner frames (GRO/GSO bug). We should open a kernel bug and try a quick kernel rollback on a small canary to confirm.
netbot: Incident created #INC-4821: "intermittent east-west geneve packet drops on gpu pool" — assigned to eng-infra.
Devon: plan: 1) collect full pcap from both ends (outer + inner) for a 5m window; 2) roll back kernel on 2 canary nodes in us-west-2a; 3) test with offloads disabled to verify mitigation; 4) file bug with kernel vendor + NIC driver.
Ravi: add `tcpdump -w /tmp/geneve-node1.pcap -i eth0 udp port 6081 or 'not ip'` and inner capture via container `nsenter -t $(pidof containerd) -n tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/inner.pcap`.
Ashley: uploaded pcaps to /mnt/ops-shared/INC-4821/geneve-node1.pcap and /geneve-node2.pcap. Also included `ip -s link` and `ethtool -k` outputs.
Caleb: rolled kernel back on canary-01 and canary-02 to 5.10.95 and re-enabled offloads — drops returned to baseline. So regression confirmed to v5.10.102.
Devon: good signal. Next: schedule larger rollback or target vendor/kernel patch. Also consider permanent workaround of setting geneve MTU to match physical path (9000) or disabling GSO on tunnel in our kube CNI init until patch lands. Tradeoffs: CPU cost vs packet loss impact.
Ashley: temporary change: kube-daemonset applying `ethtool -K geneve0 gso off gro off tso off` on gpu nodes via init script. Rolling now to 10% -> 50% -> 100% if stable.
netbot: Deploy: daemonset-offload-toggle rolled 10% at 04:12 UTC — success.
Devon: keep monitoring for packet drops and application errors. I'll open vendor bug with kernel/driver log bundle and link INC-4821.
Ravi: also ask infra to check if any SR-IOV/VF caching or RDMA path touches these nodes; RDMA offloads can interact badly with encapsulation offloads.
Ashley: FYI after the daemonset change, the grpc stream errors dropped to near-zero in the last 30m. We'll keep the workaround and await vendor patch.
Caleb: nice work everyone. Postmortem + timeline in INC-4821 when we have vendor response.
